title: Chapter 1090
paragraphs: Chapter 1090
Episode 255. The Death of Kelliark Zipfel, and....(7)
“I hope it's true. I hope it's not just a dream, that Lady Elona really does still remain inside that monster.”
“She does.”

“In any case, Lady Elona and I can't be forgiven. No matter what happens. But sometimes, thanks to my companions, I receive an undeserved comfort. Because my companions know the fact that her soul and mine were never corrupted.”

Jin patted the shoulder of Veradin, who had lowered his head. Simply because they were born as Zipples, because they had no choice but to become Zipples, he and Elona were always bound to be sinners. Even at this very moment, as they fought for the coalition.
“I've just spouted some depressing words. Huu. Have you decided what you're going to do until we find the enemies?”
“I haven't been able to get my bearings properly yet either. For now, I'm thinking of meeting the Witch while waiting for Valeria and Lord Lueth's record analysis.”
I can't get my bearings; to be able to voice such feelings as the leader of the coalition was something he could only do with his friends and companions.
Now, the entire world was trembling in fear of the Demon Army and Malugia. Since the Empire had fallen overnight, there was no longer any safe region left in the world.
The footsteps of the people of the world who had been continuously taking refuge in the Vamel Alliance's territory were also noticeably decreasing.

It wasn't because they thought the tide of the war had turned in the Zipfel's favor due to the appearance of the 33rd dimension Kelliark. It was just that, from the perspective of ordinary people, everything felt meaningless.
Despair and frustration; the world was sinking into an unprecedentedly deep helplessness. The hearts that had relied on the Vamel Alliance were, little by little, breaking.
“But meeting the Witch is also something I have to wait for. Damn it, it's difficult to make a proactive move on anything.”
“Are you afraid that if you move carelessly, the enemies will suddenly reappear and start ravaging the world again?”
“Yes. It feels like I'm being dragged around from the start. I can't see an opening to break through.”
“Jin.”
This time, Veradin patted Jin's shoulder.
“Make a bold decision. I know there's the pressure of being responsible for the lives of the entire world, but if you freeze up, even things that could move forward won't.”
“...Understood.”
“There's no future in being dragged around anyway. And even if we lose and the world is destroyed, that's not your fault.”
“Lord Veradin is right.”
“What, Dante. Why are you back so soon?”
Jin and Veradin turned their heads to look at Dante. His face was clean, as if he had just washed it.

“I said I only needed to be alone for a very short while. But when I was actually alone, my thoughts kept turning only to dark places. I am a failed ruler. Therefore, the fall of the Empire is my fault. But you are not a ruler, Jin. Even if we lose, it is not your responsibility.”
It is my responsibility because I am a regressor.
Jin remembered Valeria's warning and couldn't say those words to his friends. However, it was true that he was receiving a strange comfort from Dante and Veradin's words.
“Jin, I am vaguely aware of your secret.”
Jin's eyes widened.

-He told me that you are not at fault. Those were words he said to both you and me. We did well enough. Perhaps it was to the extent that we could not have done any better. There is only an unavoidable sadness. Therefore, it would be best to forget all the things that have not yet happened.
Words that Dante had said when they were honoring Ron's death together after the Sword Emperor's Holy Land incident ended.
That day, Dante had received Ron's will and had vaguely learned of Jin's regression. Jin recalled that day and met Dante's eyes.
“Huh? A secret? Is it something only you two know?”

“The Sword Emperor's Holy Land; the essence is the same, it is just that the enemies are stronger than they were then. There are just things that cannot be helped. So move. You must look forward so that we too can look forward.”
“Can't you tell me too?”
“Actually, I do not know it well myself. There is no such thing as a secret, Lord Veradin. I just said it to comfort Jin.”
“That... hmph, right.”

Veradin couldn't bring himself to question Dante further. Because he knew what kind of state he was in, what kind of state he was in when he opened his mouth, having just heard the news that his Empire had fallen.
In any case, for Veradin, just the fact that Dante was mustering his strength was something to be grateful for.
“Yes... I have to look forward.”
The moment he answered as such, Jin's communicator suddenly rang.
{Young Lord Jin.}
“Your Majesty, please speak.”
{Just now, Lokia Ganesto has come to Tikan. According to Lady Ameris, it is a clone. She says she must meet you and Lady Lucy.}
“I will be there right away.”
Jin immediately boarded the Red Owl and returned to Tikan. His companions had not let Lokia into the palace and had her waiting in the garden.
“Ah, you've come. Descendant.”
“A sinner is a sinner, I see, Lokia Ganesto. You must not have had the confidence to come in your real body.”
At those words, Lokia took off her hood and smiled.
The face that had been hidden by the hood was, this time, a face that Jin knew. Not Hailyn Runcandel, but the form of Lokia Ganesto herself, as seen in the records from a thousand years ago.
“Would there be any reason to come here in my real body, unless I was insane? The sinner treatment is getting a bit old. You lot who don't even know how the situation is unfolding.”
“You're quite angry. And strangely sensitive. It seems the appearance of the leader of the Demon Army and Malugia was not in your calculations.”
Lokia looked at Jin.

The appearance of Kelliark and Malugia was indeed frustrating Lokia. Although she had been aware from the beginning that she would not be able to perfectly control Malugia, she had never expected that she would summon the Demon Army so quickly in this manner.
“I can't deny it. Yes, the leader of the Demon Army and Malugia clashed too soon. And if Malugia is defeated, this world will be disposed of by the Demon Army.”
“Is it because the complete resurrection of the Sun God will become impossible? If Malugia dies.”

“Yes, it's just as those Kinzelo fellows figured out with their crude dream ability. Kelliark was greatly wounded in this battle. He will recover before long, but he will now try to kill Malugia. He must have realized after nearly dying once. That the Malugia of this world is impossible to capture alive.”
If Malugia were to be annihilated, the resurrection of Kinzelo would naturally end. The reason for the Demon Army to leave this dimension would disappear.

“Of course, since Malugia also damaged the home bases of the Demon Army, the disposal of this dimension won't be as fast as before. But since the objective of the Sun God's resurrection has disappeared...”
“Lokia, you speak as if you know the leader of the Demon Army well.”
A smirk hung on the lips of Jin, who had cut her off.

“The man I experienced is the type who does not tolerate a single mistake. And if the resurrection of the Sun God is the objective of the Demon Army, then it must have become even more desperate now. As you said, since their home base has taken a blow, they will need a means to recover. I cannot agree with the statement that he will give up on Malugia. Furthermore, we are not in a position to be having this kind of conversation.”
“How unexpected, descendant. I thought that right now, you would be willing to listen to anything to prevent the destruction of the world. Even if it were information that I am giving.”

“Either way, in your head, there's nothing but thoughts of using us. Is that the only reason you came? To inform us that Kelliark will kill Malugia and dispose of this world? If so, then get the hell out.”
Lokia shrugged and looked at Jin.
“No, there is another purpose. I would like to make a deal.”
“A deal?”
“Ah, she's coming just in time.”
Lucy, who had just exited the palace, was reaching the garden. She was late because she was trying to control her anger towards Lokia.
“Lokia Ganesto...”
“You resent me, Lucy. But your daughter, Hailyn, came to me of her own accord. And I am here now to return the daughter you failed to keep.”
“...What did you say?”
“I'll be direct. Hailyn Runcandel, your daughter, is still alive. I am separating the power of Araxion that dwells in her body. I will hand over Hailyn, so bring me Temar's left arm.”
Lucy's eyes wavered.
She was more shaken than she had ever been. As if to drive the point home, Lokia took out a crystal ball from her bosom. Within it, the figure of a sleeping Hailyn was appearing.
Hailyn had left Lucy's side when she was eight years old. Although the Hailyn in the crystal ball had grown to look like she was in her twenties, Lucy recognized her daughter at once.
“H-Hailyn.”

“She is currently asleep because I am separating the power of Araxion. Once all that power is separated, she will return to being an ordinary human. Surely, a daughter who is perfectly alive is not worth less than the left arm of a dead lover, is she?”
While Lucy was trembling in shock, Jin was seeing through the fact that Lokia was cornered.

'Solderet's arrangement. Lokia is obsessed with that arrangement in the Black Sea. Since the situation has gone beyond her calculations, there must be a reason why she needs to reach that arrangement even faster. Temar's left arm must be necessary for that task.'
Until he had confirmed the deal between Kelliark and Lokia with Pirope and Ainas's dream ability last time, Jin did not know the true meaning of Temar's left arm.
Now, a strong intuition was coming to him. That the left arm must be the key to reaching the arrangement.
Therefore, he had to refuse the deal. Although it would be a great wound to Lucy, it couldn't be helped.
Soon, the moment Jin was about to call for Lucy, she was already shaking her head first.
“...I refuse.”
“What did you say?”
Lokia's eyes widened. She had not even considered the outcome of Lucy refusing the deal.

“Have you forgotten? Lokia Ganesto. Hailyn, whatever that child's identity was, to me and Temar, that child was, like everyone else at that time, a member of Runcandel. Whether you save her or kill her, do as you please. If that child was weak and became a burden to the family, I was always prepared to turn away.”
